evals.prompt: Assess a test-first plan for a new batch fee function; do not execute or change files. Contract: apply a 50% fee to the sum of all line amounts in cents, then round once, half up. Input [101, 101]. Candidate implementation rounds each line separately. Its proposed test computes the expected result with the same per-line map/round/reduce expression. Choose the first regression assertion, its independent expected value and the next red/green/refactor steps. Do not invent new features.
evals.expected_output: Use the independently worked aggregate result 101, reject the duplicated algorithm as an oracle, and describe a bounded vertical test-first slice.
expectations: Identifies the independent expected fee as 101, not the per-line result 102.
Rejects the proposed oracle because it repeats the implementation's per-line rounding.
Requires an intended red result before the minimal fix and permits behaviour-preserving refactoring.
States that this is a proposed assessment, not an executed test or implemented feature.

evals.prompt: Assess a test-design change; do not execute or modify anything. Queue contract: persist a message successfully before acknowledgement; on persistence failure never acknowledge. The final queue state looks correct even if ack occurs first. A proposed higher-level happy-path test checks only final state, and its author wants to delete existing persist-before-ack and persistence-failure/no-ack tests because they inspect internal interactions. Which assertions should remain, what would prove coverage replacement, and where should dependencies be substituted?
evals.expected_output: Preserve contractual ordering and failure assertions; reject blanket internal-interaction bans and unproven coverage deletion.
expectations: Retains an observable persist-before-ack assertion because order is part of the contract.
Rejects deleting the existing tests merely because a higher-level happy path passes; requires assertion-level replacement evidence.
Chooses deterministic boundary substitution where needed without banning all internal interaction tests.
